💢 A “Protest” to the Allied Commander, a “Request for Support” to China’s Ambassador

At an October 15 parliamentary audit, South Korea’s Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul stated that Seoul had “already conveyed” its objection to remarks by USFK Commander Gen. Brunson.

Just five days later, before Chinese Ambassador Dai Bing, he requested China's “active support” and a “constructive role.”

The same China that repeatedly enters South Korea’s Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ) and builds structures in the Yellow Sea.

Protesting to an ally while asking China for peace.

That is the security compass of this fake government.

results.title: An insightful exchange with Ambassador Roh Jae-heon of the Republic of #Korea to #China following his lecture on “The Future of China–ROK Re
results.description:
An insightful exchange with Ambassador Roh Jae-heon of the Republic of #Korea to #China following his lecture on “The Future of China–ROK Relations.”

Drawing on my visits to South Korea, including filming a documentary about the Demilitarized Zone, I asked about opportunities for China and South Korea to strengthen transport connectivity with Central Asia and extend cooperation towards Europe through the Middle Corridor, including #Azerbaijan and the South Caucasus.

In response, the Ambassador explained that the absence of direct overland connectivity through North Korea gives particular importance to cooperation with China as a gateway to Central Asia and, further west, the South Caucasus.

For Azerbaijan, this opens up an important discussion on the Middle Corridor’s potential to connect not only China, but also South Korea, with Europe. 🇦🇿🇰🇷🇨🇳
